## Approach

For this assignment, I will use the IMDb Top 250 Movies dataset to explore movie ratings.

My research question is: **How do IMDb movie ratings compare across release decades?**

At first, I will import the CSV file into R studio. Then, I will use dplyr to select movie titles, release years, and ratings. I will remove missing values and group movies by decade, such as the 1990s, 2000s, and 2010s.

Next, I will calculate the average IMDb rating for each decade. Then, I use ggplot2 to create a graph to compare the results.

This project will help me practice cleaning, organizing, summarizing, and visualizing data using Tidyverse packages.

## Code Base

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

movies <- read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Maximus2485/Tidyverse-Vignette-Assignment.-Maxim.-Data-607/refs/heads/main/imdb_top_250_movies.csv")

# Lets select useful columns and remove missing values
movies_clean <- movies %>%
  select(primaryTitle, startYear, averageRating) %>%
  filter(!is.na(startYear), !is.na(averageRating)) %>%
#I used mutate() to create a new column called Decade. This code changes each movie's release year into its decade. For example, a movie released in 1994 belongs to the 1990s. This helps me compare movie ratings across different decades.
  mutate(Decade = (startYear %/% 10) * 10)


# Find the average rating for each decade
decade_summary <- movies_clean %>%
  group_by(Decade) %>%
  summarise(
    Movie_Count = n(),
    Average_Rating = mean(averageRating),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

decade_summary

# Create a graph
ggplot(decade_summary, aes(x = Decade, y = Average_Rating)) +
  geom_line(color = "blue") +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  labs(
    title = "Average IMDb Rating by Decade",
    x = "Release Decade",
    y = "Average Rating"
  )

```

## Conclusion

Thus, the graph shows the average IMDb movie ratings by decade. The 1990s have the highest average rating, around 8.41, while the 1920s have the lowest average rating, around 8.13.

The ratings change slightly across different decades, but most average ratings are between 8.2 and 8.4.

This shows that highly rated movies come from many different decades. However, there is no clear pattern showing that newer movies always have higher ratings than older movies.
